canonical_title: Anthropic warns of Claude session hijacking via commodity infostealers
treatment: Covered as a user-account security incident involving stolen authenticated Claude sessions. Do not repeat generic infostealer guidance without a material incident or mitigation delta.
known_facts: Anthropic warned affected Claude users that commodity infostealer malware on already-compromised devices had stolen active Claude login sessions and that a bad actor was using those sessions to consume account usage.
Anthropic identified Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine and Acreed on Windows and Atomic Stealer on a small number of Macs among malware seen in affected cases.
Anthropic said it was revoking compromised sessions, removing saved payment methods and refunding charges it identified as unauthorized.
The incident does not indicate that Claude installed or delivered the malware; Anthropic said the malware was general-purpose infostealer software already present on victims' machines.
reinclude_only_if: Anthropic publishes a formal incident report or quantified scope affecting materially more users.
Anthropic changes session-token design, device binding, authentication or account-security controls in response.
A new malware campaign or reproducible finding materially changes the practical risk or mitigation.
notes: BleepingComputer published the report at the late edge of the 2026-08-30 night coverage window and reproduced details from Anthropic emails sent to affected users.
